stem: Transition elements behave as catalysts and can form complex ions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why transition elements behave as catalysts.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Silver forms the linear complex ion $ [\text{Ag(CN)}_2]^- $.

Copper forms the tetrahedral complex ion $ [\text{Cu(CN)}_4]^{3-} $.

Titanium forms the complex $ [\text{TiCl}_4(\textit{diars})_2] $, where $ \textit{diars} $ is a neutral bidentate ligand.
parts.text: State the oxidation state and the coordination number of titanium in $ [\text{TiCl}_4(\textit{diars})_2] $.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
(c)(i)
parts.stem: The numerical value of the stability constant, $ K_{\text{stab}} $, of the copper(I) complex $ [\text{Cu(CN)}_4]^{3-} $ is $ 2.0 \times 10^{27} $.
parts.text: Write an expression for the $ K_{\text{stab}} $ of $ [\text{Cu(CN)}_4]^{3-} $.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
In a solution the concentrations of $ \text{CN}^- $ and $ [\text{Cu(CN)}_4]^{3-} $ are both $ 0.0010\text{ mol dm}^{-3} $.

Use your expression from (c)(i) and the value of $ K_{\text{stab}} $ to calculate the concentration of $ \text{Cu}^+\text{(aq)} $ in this solution.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
A piece of a copper-containing alloy has a mass of $ 0.567\text{ g} $. It is dissolved in an acid giving $ 100.0\text{ cm}^3 $ of a blue solution in which all the copper is present as $ \text{Cu}^{2+} $ ions.

An excess of $ \text{KI(aq)} $ is added to a $ 25.0\text{ cm}^3 $ sample of this solution.

All of the copper is precipitated as white $ \text{CuI(s)} $.

$ \text{Cu}^{2+} $ ions are the only component in the solution that react with $ \text{KI(aq)} $. This is reaction 1.

reaction 1 $$2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4\text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{CuI} + \text{I}_2$$

The liberated $ \text{I}_2 $ is then titrated with $ 0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3} $ $ \text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} $. This is reaction 2.

reaction 2 $$\text{I}_2 + 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{I}^- + \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$$

The titration requires $ 20.10\text{ cm}^3 $ of $ 0.0200\text{ mol dm}^{-3} $ $ \text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} $ to reach the end-point.
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of $ \text{I}_2 $ that are reduced in this titration.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of copper in the original piece of alloy.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the percentage of copper in the alloy.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: Suggest why a solution of $ \text{Cu}^{2+} $ is coloured but solid $ \text{CuI} $ is white.
